courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
courses.contributionFinding: Academic reading/writing/research literacy, reflection and personal development. Required Year1 foundation; broader than ThriveTrack.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courses.evidenceRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
courses.contributionFinding: AIapplications,labourmarkets,inequality,productivity andregulation provide specific context for changingwork andorganisations. A countryAIreadiness/workforce/regulation/industrial-policyproject is not psychological diagnosis or adedicatedHRanalytics course.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
courses.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
courses.contributionFinding: adds microeconomic and behavioural analysis of individual and institutional decision-making
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Behavioral Economics
courses.evidenceRead: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
courses.contributionFinding: connects psychological evidence to economic decision-making, biases and behavioural choice
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Market Research
courses.evidenceRead: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas. Ready to turn curiosity into career skills? Perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
courses.contributionFinding: provides applied research design, data gathering and analysis in organisational and market contexts
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: International Business & Governance
courses.evidenceRead: Examines how international trade, globalization and political, sociocultural and technological forces shape firms' cross-border decisions. Economic foundations include trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and the monetary system. Students analyze governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate an international-business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy covering country attractiveness and business functions. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices and negotiation.
courses.contributionFinding: examines institutional and cultural forces, corporate responsibility and international business governance as complementary organisational context, not psychological diagnosis
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.
courses.contributionFinding: develops a venture through teamwork, design thinking and market validation, providing an applied business context for later organisational and market-research study
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
courses.contributionFinding: provides foundational empirical research design and statistical analysis
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Personal Leadership
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces leadership through self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Covey's habits provide a framework for personal vision, prioritization and collaboration, alongside transformational, authentic, situational and adaptive leadership perspectives. Students analyze personality and emotional-intelligence profiles in relation to group dynamics, examine leadership cases, and construct a personal development plan with actionable goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection rather than diagnosis, and the outline acknowledges differences in their scientific support.
courses.contributionFinding: provides foundational leadership theory, self-awareness and applied leadership skills
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Leadership Communication
courses.evidenceRead: Studies leadership communication through leadership theory, persuasion and practical rhetorical work. Students compare contemporary leadership approaches and examine emotional intelligence, gender, culture and ethics. Literary characters, film and speeches provide material for analyzing effective and ineffective leadership. Students interview a real leader, analyze the leader's communication challenge in an advisory report, and develop a public address presenting their own ethical leadership vision.
courses.contributionFinding: develops leadership communication, ethics and interpersonal influence
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
courses.evidenceRead: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, emotional expression and suppression, emotional labor, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership and social interaction under conflict, exclusion and interpersonal uncertainty. It emphasises inclusive leadership and ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender minority experiences, with digital emotion regulation as a further strand. Students conduct a supervised quantitative survey project: formulating theory-driven hypotheses, selecting established psychological measures, designing and piloting a Qualtrics survey, recruiting participants ethically, collecting original data and preparing a clean dataset. Individual work applies descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio, and interprets findings and limitations in empirical reports and evidence-based leadership recommendations.
courses.contributionFinding: Emotion regulation,emotional labour,belonging,identity safety andinclusive leadership give direct psychological study of work andsocial interaction. A supervised survey develops hypotheses,measurement,piloting,ethical recruitment,originaldata analysis andempiricalreports.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
courses.evidenceRead: Examines organizational behaviour at individual, group and organizational levels. Topics connect personality, perception, emotions and motivation to teams, leadership, power, conflict, structure, culture and change. Students design research plans for organizational cases and conduct a brief systematic literature review using PRISMA reporting tools. Workshops develop literature searching, study selection, source appraisal and synthesis, linking organizational-psychology evidence to practical questions and recommendations.
courses.contributionFinding: provides organisational-psychology theory on motivation, leadership, groups and organisational culture
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
courses.evidenceRead: Develops negotiation as an analytical practice and interpersonal skill. Students learn interest-based bargaining, BATNA and ZOPA, value creation, framing, concessions and strategies for handling power, emotions and difficult counterparts. Social-psychological and communication perspectives connect negotiation to trust, ethics, culture and relationships. Frequent simulations and narrative analysis lead to an annotated negotiation film and the design, teaching and evaluation of a negotiation scenario grounded in Delta Climate Center themes.
courses.contributionFinding: develops negotiation, strategic interaction and the psychology of influence
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
courses.contributionFinding: R-based data import,cleaning,joining,transformation andvisualisation directly develop empiricaldataprocessing. A studentproject supplies researchpractice without presuming apsychologydataset.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.
courses.contributionFinding: teaches regression, classification, clustering and predictive model evaluation as computational methods complementary to cognitive research, without claiming a neuroscience dataset
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
courses.evidenceRead: Examines how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognize structures and objects. Spatial and spectral representations, colour and image statistics support filtering, segmentation, curve and feature detection, tracking and object classification. Students use Python and OpenCV to implement image-processing techniques, investigate spectral representations, and build a recognition pipeline whose performance is benchmarked on previously unseen images.
courses.contributionFinding: studies algorithms that model visual recognition and extract structure from images; this is a computational comparison with human vision rather than neural-perception training
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python. Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.
courses.contributionFinding: provides Python programming and computational problem-solving foundations for the selected data and computer-vision methods
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces major philosophical questions through close study of arguments from ancient Greek thought to contemporary philosophy, with a related Buddhist perspective on the self. Students examine knowledge, ethics, God, mind and consciousness, freedom, identity, time and meaning. Historical texts and contemporary debates, including AI consciousness and concepts of race and gender, develop the ability to reconstruct, evaluate and formulate philosophical arguments in focused essays.
courses.contributionFinding: introduces epistemology, consciousness and philosophical reasoning as preparation for the selected focused philosophy-of-mind courses
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.evidenceRead: Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.
courses.contributionFinding: develops moral reasoning about responsibility, motivation and practical ethical questions; it complements but does not replace professional psychological ethics
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Philosophy of Mind
courses.evidenceRead: Examines minds, selves and conscious experience through historical and contemporary philosophy. Personal identity and self-knowledge are considered alongside Buddhist accounts and neuropsychological cases. Behaviourism, physicalism, functionalism and their critics frame the mind-body problem. Later inquiries address machine consciousness, virtual worlds, dreaming, perception, transformative experience and the value of experience. Essays develop independent philosophical interpretations and arguments.
courses.contributionFinding: examines consciousness, personal identity, mind-body explanations and animal/machine minds as philosophical contributions to the study of cognition
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courses.evidenceRead: Examines what emotions are and how they shape knowledge, decision-making, ethics, social life and politics. Feeling, cognitive and perceptual theories are compared with historical, phenomenological and contemporary accounts. Love, fear, grief, moods and political anger provide focused cases, alongside emotions in art and their changing relation to time. Students analyze texts and emotional vignettes and develop an independent philosophical paper or a project combining argument with creative work.
courses.contributionFinding: examines the nature of emotions, their relation to perception and belief, and their rationality; this complements empirical psychology with philosophical analysis
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
courses.evidenceRead: Explores free will and agency in relation to time and the self. Historical Greek and Indian perspectives introduce debates about fatalism, determinism, compatibility and moral responsibility; later topics include scientific challenges, addiction, luck and agency in games. The second part examines the reality and experience of time, physics and temporal asymmetries, then developing research linking time, action and selfhood. Essays require close source analysis and an independent argument.
courses.contributionFinding: examines agency, free will, time and selfhood as philosophical questions about the interpretation of human choice
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces sociological reasoning through classical theories, their historical settings and perspectives that address exclusions from the discipline. Students connect solidarity, modernity, identity, social boundaries, networks and stratification to race, gender, migration and inequality in education and work. An individual analysis applies a course concept to contemporary social life without original data collection. A group paper develops a sociological question and analyzes a social problem using theory and academic literature.
courses.contributionFinding: examines social institutions and classical theories, complementing psychological accounts of how social settings influence behaviour
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.evidenceRead: Develops qualitative inquiry from research design and preparation through data collection, management, analysis and dissemination. Students examine methodological foundations, ethics, positionality and reflexivity alongside interviews, focus groups, ethnography, documentary and visual approaches. Coding, thematic interpretation and NVivo support analysis. Research teams formulate a question, collect and analyze qualitative evidence, and report their methodological decisions, findings and limitations in staged assignments.
courses.contributionFinding: provides qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation skills
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Modern Sociology
courses.evidenceRead: Examines twentieth-century and contemporary social theory alongside critical accounts of modernity, colonialism and disciplinary exclusion. Functionalism, critical theory, Black feminist thought, phenomenology, symbolic interactionism and Bourdieu's work are read with postcolonial, decolonial and Indigenous perspectives. Students compare theories and apply them to empirical cases, including visual material. An individual research paper develops a theoretically grounded interpretation of a selected social phenomenon.
courses.contributionFinding: examines modernity, colonialism and social theory as structural and historical perspectives complementary to social psychology
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.evidenceRead: Focuses on civil society through critical, neo-functionalist and decolonial social theory. Students examine social trust, capital, hegemony, public spheres, solidarity, social movements and civil repair across political and regional contexts. An experience report relates personal engagement or observation to course concepts. An individual research project uses theoretical and empirical sources to analyze a civil-society organization, movement, initiative or related phenomenon.
courses.contributionFinding: studies civil society, solidarity, social trust and collective life, adding an explicitly sociological perspective on social behaviour
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Neurobiology
courses.evidenceRead: Studies nervous systems and behaviour from comparative, evolutionary and physiological perspectives. Brain anatomy and laboratory introductions support analysis of animal behaviour, research models and welfare. The second part connects regulatory behaviour and biological rhythms to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. Comparative-anatomy work and a literature-based disorder report apply neurobiological concepts while animal-research assignments examine reduction, refinement and replacement.
courses.contributionFinding: provides neurobiological foundations for understanding cognition and brain-behaviour relations
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Perception & Action
courses.evidenceRead: Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
courses.contributionFinding: examines neural mechanisms of perception and action
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Higher Order Functions
courses.evidenceRead: Deepens understanding of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and the experimental study of higher cognitive functions. Students examine attention, memory, emotion, cognitive control, social cognition, pain and consciousness, connecting brain function and dysfunction to behaviour. An attentional-blink experiment provides direct engagement with empirical work. A team research proposal requires literature analysis, a feasible experimental design and ethical reflection, supported by peer review.
courses.contributionFinding: develops advanced understanding of memory, attention, executive functions and higher cognition
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.evidenceRead: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
courses.contributionFinding: examines language processing through psychological and neurobiological perspectives
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science. Students study biological molecules, cells and membranes, communication, enzymes and energy metabolism, cell division, DNA and heredity, gene expression, genomes and biotechnology. Scientific experiments and papers are analyzed through short teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium. A responsive final component selects additional life- and biomedical-science topics with the class.
courses.contributionFinding: provides cell signalling, genetics and cellular physiology foundations for the biological study of the nervous system; it is a life-science foundation rather than a psychology course
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes. Students study neural signalling, brain anatomy and development, learning, intelligence, personality, social influence, mental disorders and treatments. Several sessions introduce behavioural, imaging and electrophysiological approaches to neuroscience and their combined use. Interdisciplinary research-article and case analysis connects psychological processes to neural mechanisms and clinical questions.
courses.contributionFinding: provides the foundational psychology and neuroscience gateway for advanced behavioural and cognitive courses
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Human Physiology
courses.evidenceRead: Studies normal function and regulation in the adult human body, linking molecular and cellular processes to integrated organ systems. Homeostasis, signalling and energy handling frame nervous, endocrine, muscular, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, digestive and reproductive functions. Medical examples illustrate physiological principles. An individual literature-based paper examines a selected physiological or pathophysiological process and is developed through structured peer review and revision.
courses.contributionFinding: examines nervous and endocrine systems, signalling and integrated bodily regulation within normal human physiology, complementing neurobiology
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Social Psychology
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
courses.contributionFinding: provides core social-psychology theory on attitudes, groups and interpersonal behaviour
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courses.evidenceRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.
courses.contributionFinding: provides advanced statistical and experimental methods for psychological research
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Psychopathology
courses.evidenceRead: Examines mental health and psychopathology across the lifespan using a biopsychosocial perspective. Historical views, classification and assessment frame biological, psychological, cultural and social explanations of disorders and treatment. Case-based work applies diagnostic concepts to varied presentations. A structured literature-based essay investigates a focused mental-health question through explicit searching, source selection, evidence appraisal and synthesis, with optional use of PRISMA reporting tools.
courses.contributionFinding: examines mental disorders through psychological and biopsychosocial perspectives
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Medical & Health Psychology
courses.evidenceRead: Examines health and illness through interactions among biological, psychological and sociocultural factors. Health inequalities, behaviour and prevention lead into stress, symptoms, pain, medical consultation and treatment decisions. Chronic illness is considered from patients', families' and healthcare professionals' perspectives. Students analyze research, interventions and clinical cases, practice interviewing with attention to culture, and apply clinical-health formulation to understand support and quality of life in medical settings.
courses.contributionFinding: examines psychological determinants of health, illness and wellbeing using a biopsychosocial approach
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
courses.evidenceRead: Introduces clinical psychological assessment and major psychotherapeutic approaches across the lifespan. Students study ethics, diagnostic systems, test reliability and validity, interviews, personality and cognitive assessment, then psychodynamic, behavioural, cognitive, humanistic, systemic and integrative treatments. Training sessions develop introductory administration, scoring and interpretation skills. A psychodiagnostic case report integrates findings and treatment recommendations, while self-monitoring examines developing clinical skills.
courses.contributionFinding: Lifespan clinicalassessment,ethicaldiagnostics,measurementvalidity,interviewing andpsychotherapies provide substantial appliedpsychology. Training andcase-report recommendations do not establish professional qualification or aguaranteed child-onlycase.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
courses.evidenceRead: Teaches systematic review and meta-analysis for synthesizing evidence in medical, behavioural and related research. Students define review questions, search and select studies, extract and code findings, assess bias and compute effect sizes. Hands-on R work fits fixed- and random-effects models, examines heterogeneity and moderators, conducts meta-regression and investigates publication bias. A group project completes a small meta-analysis and presents its methods and results in a research poster.
courses.contributionFinding: Systematicreviews andmeta-analysis develop questionformulation,search/selection,coding,bias assessment,effect sizes,heterogeneity andmetaregression inR. This is direct empirical-evidencesynthesis,not a generic advancedseminar or guaranteed originalpsychologicalexperiment.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
courses.evidenceRead: Examines physical, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development from prenatal life through old age and death. Biological and environmental influences are considered alongside attachment, education, relationships, cultural differences and developmental psychopathology. Students connect theoretical perspectives to case studies, assessment and interventions at different life stages. A life-story interview with an adult over fifty applies developmental concepts through interviewing, analysis and a written report.
courses.contributionFinding: provides systematic study of cognitive, emotional and social development across the lifespan
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
courses.evidenceRead: Examines youth radicalization and educational prevention through psychology, education, sociology, political science and peace education. Models of radicalization and adolescent risk and protective factors lead into inclusive school climates, belonging, social-emotional learning, dialogue, media literacy and civic agency. Students translate primary research into teacher-training materials and a youth toolkit for an international school project, then revise the resources using feedback from intended recipients.
courses.contributionFinding: Youth radicalization andeducationalprevention connect adolescentrisk/protection,inclusive schoolclimates,social-emotionallearning,dialogue andmedia literacy. Actualteacher-trainingmaterials andayouth toolkit are revisedwithrecipientfeedback; no generic schoolpsychologist qualification is implied.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

courses.name: Persuasive Communication
courses.evidenceRead: Examines contemporary persuasion through communication studies, social psychology and ethical analysis, then applies it in community-engaged work. Students study coactive persuasion, framing, argumentation, cognitive shortcuts and verbal and nonverbal communication. Projects with the Delta Climate Centre and Vlissingen municipality develop communication encouraging sustainable and circular lifestyles. An individual research paper evaluates selected persuasion tools through literature review, field research diaries and reflective analysis of their use.
courses.contributionFinding: Social-psychological theories ofpersuasion,framing,argumentation andcognitive shortcuts supply specific applied behaviour/influence study. Communityprojects concern sustainable/circularlifestyles; they are not asserted as internalHRprojects.
courses.role: Direct psychology/empiricalmethods orspecific complementarybiological,philosophical,computational,social ororganisational subject; not disciplinaryequivalence.

concepts.label: Psychology, behaviour & social contexts
concepts.concept: Social, developmental, clinical and cognitive psychology are studied through empirical research and evidence synthesis. Organisational psychology, biological foundations, behavioural economics and social theory add distinct perspectives on people, mental processes and social settings.

concepts.label: Brain, cognition & mind
concepts.concept: Brain and behaviour, perception, memory and language form the centre of this programme. Neuroscience and psychology connect with data analysis and computational models of vision, while philosophy examines consciousness, emotion and the self.

concepts.label: Psychology, leadership & organisations
concepts.concept: Psychology of work and organisations connects with leadership, diversity, negotiation, behavioural decision-making and empirical research. Sociology and business courses examine the institutional settings in which people work.
